archetype.name: Fading Contender (offense in free fall)
archetype.definition: A team with a recent title-level track record, 14 wins in 2024 and 11 in 2025, now playing like a bottom-five unit while its line and skill-position core thin out.

report.headline: The record is the generous part; the play underneath is bottom-three.
report.take:
Philadelphia is 2-3, and that is kinder than the play. Net EPA ranks 30th, the offense is 29th in EPA and dead last in success rate, and only Jacksonville's 3rd-ranked defense would call 262.6 yards a game good. The two wins came by two points over Washington and four over Tennessee, the league's 31st-ranked offense, and neither covered as a 6- or 7-point favorite. Wins over expected sit at -0.65, so this isn't a good team losing coin flips. The point differential and the EPA say the same thing: this is a below-average team right now.

The offense is the root of it. The run game fails at the point of attack: 30.1% of carries are stuffed (31st) and 3.19 yards per carry ranks 28th. That leaves Jalen Hurts in long-yardage downs behind a line taking sacks on 7.2% of dropbacks. A 3.04-second time to throw (5th longest) fits a quarterback holding the ball because nothing is open early. The passing game went from +8.8 EPA against Tennessee to -16.5 in Chicago and -8.2 against the Rams, and the Jaguars game produced 22 rushing yards and -11.4 rush EPA. The line is also losing pieces. Lane Johnson, a 100%-snap starter, has retired, and center Drew Kendall is out. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are both hamstring question marks.

The defense is hiding worse numbers than its 14th-ranked scoring line suggests. It ranks 31st in pressure rate, 32nd in QB hit rate and 31st in missed tackles, with only 3 takeaways (29th). What keeps points down is a 50% red-zone TD rate allowed (6th) and few explosive runs. Both are bend-don't-break traits that usually drift back toward average. Special teams (+3.86 EPA a game, 6th) and Sirianni going for it on every fourth down are covering the margins.

The history is why nobody should write them off entirely. This roster was elite two years ago and 9th in points allowed last year, and five of the next eight opponents rank 22nd or worse on defense. But the 2025 offense had already slid to 17th in EPA, so the decline didn't start this fall. Getting Barkley and Smith back would help. It doesn't fix a line that just lost its right tackle or a front that can't hit the quarterback.

strengths.title: Special teams winning hidden yardage
strengths.body: At +3.86 EPA a game, the kicking and coverage units are roughly offsetting a chunk of the offense's deficit and turning short drives into points. Special teams value is noisier than offense or defense, but it is the most reliable thing this team has done all year.

strengths.title: Bend-don't-break in the red zone
strengths.body: Opponents are scoring touchdowns on only half their red-zone trips, and the defense rarely gives up big runs. That keeps points allowed at 14th despite a 23rd-ranked EPA defense. Without a pass rush or takeaways behind it, expect the red-zone rate to drift worse.

strengths.title: A soft middle of the schedule
strengths.body: Dallas twice (32nd in defensive EPA), Arizona (29th), Indianapolis (26th) and Washington (24th) are all ahead. That is the window for a struggling offense to find a rhythm. It is the main reason a .500 finish is still plausible.

concerns.title: Offense can't stay on schedule
concerns.body: The 32nd-ranked success rate starts with a run game getting stuffed on 30% of carries. That pushes Hurts into obvious passing downs behind a leaky line. It isn't game script, since they've run below expectation (-3.2 PROE) and still failed. Without Johnson and Kendall up front, it's hard to see the line improving.

concerns.title: No pass rush, no takeaways
concerns.body: An 11.7% pressure rate and the league's lowest QB hit rate mean quarterbacks are completing passes cleanly. Opposing WR1s and TE1s are well above their norms against this defense. Greenard is out and Hunt is questionable, so help isn't coming from the injury report, and three takeaways in five games leaves the offense no short fields.

concerns.title: Line attrition with Johnson retired
concerns.body: Losing an every-snap right tackle to retirement is permanent. Kendall's knee injury also weakens the interior. A line already 25th in sack rate, protecting a QB with a 3-second time to throw, is the worst setup to absorb that.

trend.note: Positive passing EPA in Weeks 1-2 gave way to -16.5 in Chicago and -8.2 against the Rams, then the run game collapsed in London (-11.4 rush EPA). The 19-17 loss to Jacksonville was competitive against a top-3 defense, which is the lone sign of a floor.

nextGame.headline: Pick'em on paper, but Carolina's profile is clearly better
nextGame.body:
Carolina is the more efficient team, 8th in net EPA to Philadelphia's 30th. Its offense under Bryce Young is pass-heavy (+5.9 PROE, 3rd) and productive (6th in pass EPA), which is exactly what a defense with the league's weakest pass rush struggles to stop. Carolina's line allows the league's highest pressure rate, but Philadelphia's rush is 31st in pressure rate. On the other side, Carolina's 4th-ranked pressure rate meets an Eagles line missing its right tackle and center with a quarterback who holds the ball.

Availability is the swing. Philadelphia is hopeful on Barkley and Smith, but Kendall, Greenard and Epps are out, Hunt and Carter are questionable, and Shipley is doubtful, which thins the backfield further if Barkley sits. Carolina is coming off a bye with Etienne expected back and Coker on track. Its tackle room is depleted, with Ekwonu and Moton out and Freeling questionable, but that matters less against a front that doesn't get home.

keyMatchups.title: Panthers pressure vs patched-up Eagles line
keyMatchups.body: Carolina pressures on 26% of dropbacks while Philadelphia's quarterback averages over three seconds to throw. With a new right tackle and a backup center, long-developing dropbacks become sacks and drive-killers.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Carolina sees an above-average share of tight end targets and has let TE1s score 4.1 PPR points over their norm, while holding WR1s 6 under. If Philadelphia's quick-game answer exists, it runs through Goedert rather than the outside receivers.

keyMatchups.title: Carolina's air attack vs no rush
keyMatchups.body: A top-8 offense built on passing meets a defense 24th in pass EPA allowed that can't hit the quarterback. Carolina's leaky line is the Eagles' only opening, and their front hasn't shown it can exploit that.

nextGame.watch: Whether Hurts can get the ball out early against Carolina's rush. Its 27th-ranked deep-pass defense is there to be hit only if the line gives him time.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the offense to improve some, but not enough to change who this team is. Barkley and Smith returning and a run of weak defenses (Dallas twice, Arizona, Indianapolis) should lift scoring toward 20 a game. The line losses are permanent, though, and the run game's stuff rate is a structural problem. The defense is more likely to slip than improve: the red-zone stinginess and 14th-ranked scoring defense are propped up by things that regress, with no pass rush or takeaways underneath them.

A team with this profile and this schedule lands around .500 at best. The division is weak enough that 8 or 9 wins would still keep them in the race. The back end of the schedule, with Seattle's 2nd-ranked defense and an unbeaten 49ers team, limits the ceiling.
swingFactors: How the line holds without Johnson
Whether the pass rush finds any pressure

bets.reason: Carolina is 8th in net EPA to Philadelphia's 30th, and the Eagles are 1-4 against the spread with a line now missing Johnson and Kendall against a top-4 pressure defense. The market is pricing the jersey and home field, not this season's play.

Carolina's games average 57.6 combined points and its offense meets the league's weakest pass rush. Carolina has also allowed red-zone TDs at a 72.7% rate. The caution is Philadelphia's broken offense, and Carolina's league-best +1.3 turnover margin per game is unlikely to hold.

confidence.note: Five games, but the offensive decline shows up across opponents and is compounded by permanent line losses.
